title: Where does the curve fit?
hook: Four flips, three candidate biases: compare the sequence probabilities.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: drag a curve's parameters; a likelihood meter peaks at the best fit.

misconception: Treating maximum likelihood as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: drag a curve's parameters; a likelihood meter peaks at the best fit.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: You observe 3 heads and 1 tail in four independent coin flips. Which bias makes this exact sequence most likely?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-maximum-likelihood/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Four independent flips contain 3 H and 1 T. Compare likelihoods p^3(1-p) for p=.25,.5,.75: .01171875,.0625,.10546875; changing the data to 1 H reverses the optimum.

src/demos/probability/p100-maximum-likelihood/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Four independent flips contain 3 H and 1 T. Compare likelihoods p^3(1-p) for p=.25,.5,.75: .01171875,.0625,.10546875; changing the data to 1 H reverses the optimum.

claims.text: The retained cases select 75% heads for three heads and 25% for one head. Each bar multiplies the probabilities of the four observed flips.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-maximum-likelihood/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Four independent flips contain 3 H and 1 T. Compare likelihoods p^3(1-p) for p=.25,.5,.75: .01171875,.0625,.10546875; changing the data to 1 H reverses the optimum.

claims.text: The tallest bar maximizes the likelihood of this sequence among these candidates. It is not the probability that the candidate bias is true; that would also require a prior.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-maximum-likelihood/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Four independent flips contain 3 H and 1 T. Compare likelihoods p^3(1-p) for p=.25,.5,.75: .01171875,.0625,.10546875; changing the data to 1 H reverses the optimum.

claims.text: For 2 heads and 2 tails, which candidate bias maximizes p²(1−p)²? The symmetric sequence has likelihood 0.0625 at 50%, larger than 0.03516 at either other candidate.
